answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 10 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The marble multiplier is published, charged in falcon, and wander lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4471 identities would post 4398 proofs and burn roughly 90 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
